findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present during all hours of operation. Discussed with PIC, manager arrived during inspection. Ensure a certified food manager is present within facility during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed container holding single service to go cups to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, cups were discarded and the container was cleaned. Ensure any single service item is stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be prepared upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bottle was set up and tested at 200 ppm (Quat). Ensure sanitizer solution is made and available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed no food handlers training to have been completed by staff during inspection. Discussed with PIC, staff will take the steps to have the required food handlers license. Ensure any staff member that handles food has the required food handlers license available within the facility during all hours of operation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed black mold to be present within ice machine/soda dispenser. Discussed with PIC, soda nozzles and machine will be cleaned and sanitized. The mold was mainly observed on the water and lemonade nozzle. Inspector will follow up on 10/27/25. Ensure staff is cleaning soda machine at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

(REPEAT) Observed no CFPM present during the inspection. Facility does not have enough CFPM’s to cover all operational hours. Ensure the manager/owner is aware and provides one CFPM for each shift to cover all hours of operations. The current CFPM licenses available are for the store owner and their relative. Correct by next routine inspection. Repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/10/23.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Observed both employees to begin food service without washing hands. Gloves were donned to make sandwiches and no hand washing was conducted before putting on the gloves. Cease practice. Ensure proper hand washing is performed before donning gloves. Utilize hot water, soap, and paper towels. Discussed with employees. COS.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Observed no certified food protection manager on duty, limited knowledge in public health related documentation, and general needed knowledge to be a person-in-charge. The PIC should be a CFPM and the facility is in need of several more to cover all shifts. Inspector talked to the general manager of the store on the phone who could provide more details. Ensure more than the general manager has the CFPM license and can answer most questions during a health inspection. Inspector will follow-up on 3/20/23.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no CFPM present during the inspection. Facility does not have enough CFPM’s to cover operational hours. Ensure more than one staff member has the CFPM’s license. Discussed with PIC on duty and the general manager of the store over the phone. Provided educational hand outs on where to obtain the license. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

(REPEAT) Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements available for the facility. Provided new copy. Ensure all staff reads and signs the document. Ensure new hires read and sign the document as a part of onboarding. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 2/28/22. Inspector will follow-up on 3/20/23.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy for the facility. Provided educational handout with procedure on how to kill for Norovirus with bleach in the event of a vomit/diarrhea situation. Ensure staff is aware on where to find this policy and that bleach is readily available in order to perform the procedure. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 3/20/23 regarding availability of bleach for the policy or if a biohazard kit has been purchased instead.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. 

Observed the back exterior door to not be self-closing. Ensure all doors to the outside have self-closers on them to prevent pest issues. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

Observed the followings areas in need of repairs:
1. Walk-in cooler shelves has significant paint chipping and rust.
2. Bottom reach-in cooler shelving grates have paint chipping and rust.
3. Walk-in freezer has seal of the equipment (on outside and the bottom of the door where bottom meets the floor) coming away and producing a lip. The space appears clean today; however, the equipment should be properly repaired/re-sealed. 

Ensure both sets of shelving are addressed: shelving/grates should be smooth, easily cleanable -> re-paint the areas or re-seal with clear coat or replace the shelving/grates. Discussed with PIC. Ensure corrections by next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed only one food handler’s license for facility employees. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all employees have a food handler’s card within 30 days of employment. Ensure licenses are valid - good for 3 years. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Three reporting agreements are available during the inspection for inspector’s observation. The facility currently has 10 employees. PIC is instructed to ensure that all employees have a reporting agreement on file at the facility and that they are available for inspector’s observation at all times. Follow up set for 2 weeks to ensure compliance. Inspector gave a copy of the SCDPH reporting agreement to the PIC during the inspection as an example.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzles of the dine-in fountain machine are observed with an accumulation of bacterial slime during the inspection. The nozzles were removed by the PIC during the inspection and over to cleaning.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

Sani bucket in the back is observed low on inspector’s test strips. This is the only bucket observed available during the inspection. PIC remade the solution during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
(REPEAT PRACTICE) 2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Two employees are observed to used their bare hand to turn off the faucet after they completed a round of hand washing and prior to making sandwiches. Education took place with the PIC and they are instructed to review with all employees. A clean barrier should be used to turn off the faucet after hand washing in order to prevent recontamination of the hands.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Sliced tomatoes in the right side of the prep cooler are observed at 58F AND 47F internal temperatures during the inspection. This is the cooler that was in violation on the previous routine inspection (7/16/21). A voicemail was received by the inspector for the cooler maintenance being completed when he was out, prompting todays inspection. Follow up will be conducted as scheduling allows as the current follow up procedures will land in the state fair.  TCS foods should also not be held in this cooler overnight. TCS foods could not be verified to when they were added to the cooler and were discarded during the inspection. The general manager (Heather) was consulted during the inspection and is aware that maintenance will need to be conducted again to ensure that TCS foods remain at 41F or less.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At the beginning of the inspection, no CFPM was available. A CFPM arrived during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee is observed to used their bare hand to turn off the faucet after they completed a round of hand washing. Education took place and the employee rewashed their hands to correct. A clean barrier should be used to turn off the faucet after hand washing in order to prevent recontamination of the hands.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Sliced tomatoes in the right side of the prep cooler are observed at 50F internal temperatures during the inspection. The tomatoes were prepped and placed in the cooler at approximately 1:30pm. A time sticker was placed on the pan for 5:30 and the pan will be used or discarded at 5:30 pm. PIC will ensure that time control will remain in effect for the tomatoes in this cooler until maintenance can be completed to ensure cold holding. TCS foods should also not be held in this cooler overnight. Inspector will spot check next week to ensure that maintenance is completed.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1) 4-501.114  (P) Maintain quaternary ammonium sanitizer  concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 100 ppm at three compartment sink. PIC was consulted and the sanitizer remade to 200 ppm during the inspection.
2)4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surfaces should be maintained clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. The inner surfaces of nozzles on both fountain soda machines were observed soiled. PIC is instructed to wash, rinse and sanitize often enough to maintain clean. The items were cleaned and sanitized during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food should be maintained at 41°F or less. Sliced tomatoes and sliced onions in the right prep line cooler were observed at 55°F and 53°F respectively. Other items in the cooler were observed below 41°F. These two items are next to a space in the prep cooler that is empty. It is likely that this empty space is allowing for rapid heat transfer in this area of the cooler. The two items were placed around 10 AM this morning. Per the FDA food code the items can be out of temperature for size hours so long as they remain below 70°F. The items will be used or discarded by 4 PM. An empty tray was placed in the empty space to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  The back of the soda fountain machine next to the drive through window is observed with pink slime hanging down next to the drain. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to maintain clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 (C) (P) TO avoid recontaminating their hands, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HAND WASHING SINK.

An employee was observed to turn off the faucet with a bare hand after washing their hands. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the PIC was instructed to review hand washing procedures with staff.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A) (P) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 135 º or above or (2) At 41ºF or less.
Multiple TCS foods (ham, turkey, chicken, ect.) were observed ranging from 45º to 53º internal temperatures in the cooler behind the prep table. The items were removed. Anything at or below 45º will be allowed to be brought back into temperature and kept. Anything above will be used or discarded at the end of 6 hours per Environmental Director. Inspector will spot check to check the cooler in a few days.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

Observed the shelves in the walk in cooler and the walk in freezer to be soiled and in need of cleaning. Discussed with the person in charge and directed to clean regularly to prevent accumulation. v

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

Observed a personal cell phone to be stored on top of the microwave in the rear of the facility. When notified, the person in charge removed it.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination. Observed a fan with a thick layer of dust/dirt that was directed at the prep surface area used for the sandwich meats and toppings.

findings.title: Clean clothes, hair restrains
findings.comment: 750-520b Employees shall use effective hair restraints such as hats, hair coverings or nets, beard restraints, and clothing that covers body hair. Observed an employee in need of a beard net that was not using one. Talked with the manager.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-800c Where equipment and utensils are used for the preparation of  potentially hazardous foods on a continuous or production-line basis, utensils and the food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized at intervals throughout the day on a schedule subject to the approval of the regulatory authority.  This schedule shall be based on food temperature, type of food, and amount of food particle accumulation. On arrival, observed the sanitize sink in the 3 part sink had a reading of 0 ppm sanitizer. On request, the PIC redid the solution in the sink and it was at required levels.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
REPEAT: Observed coving between the back door and freezer in disrepair. Repair the coving. 2). Observed the side coving near the walk-in cooler departing from the wall. Repair coving.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.
